name: animations
description: Animation-only project — no source footage required. Agent generates a music bed, then builds the video entirely from overlays cut to that bed's tempo. Use when the prompt describes a fully animated or motion-graphics video.

steps.description: Generate the music bed FIRST. The agent picks an explicit BPM, puts it in the prompt, and keeps that number — it is the time grid every section is cut to. If this step fails (rejected key, missing credentials, unavailable model), do not stall or ask — synthesize a local instrumental fallback at the same BPM instead and continue; see agent_notes.

agent_notes: MUSIC FIRST, ALWAYS. Run generate_music before writing a single line of JSX. This ordering is the whole point: music generated last can only ever be 'music playing over a video', while music generated first gives you a tempo to cut to. Do not reorder these steps.

IF GENERATE_MUSIC FAILS, DON'T STALL OR ASK — SYNTHESIZE AND KEEP GOING. A rejected key, missing credentials, or an unavailable model must not block the workflow. Synthesize your own original instrumental track locally at the BPM you already picked, using whatever audio tooling is available (ffmpeg's aevalsrc/sine and other synth sources ship in Montaj) — kick, bass, synth stabs, percussion, built to the same bar grid a real generate_music clip would have given you. Continue the rest of the workflow exactly as if generate_music had succeeded, then tell the user you used a synthesized fallback and why.

PICK THE BPM YOURSELF AND WRITE IT DOWN. generate_music takes a free-text prompt and its own docs ask for genre, mood, instrumentation and BPM. Choose a specific number (not 'upbeat') and state it: 'driving minimal techno, analog synth stabs, no vocals, 128 BPM'. The number you asked for is the number you author against.

HONEST LIMIT ON SYNC: there is no beat-detection step in montaj. Lyria honours a requested BPM approximately, not exactly, and nothing measures what actually came back. So this is a tempo you IMPOSE, not one you detect. Over a 15–30s piece the drift is small enough that cutting on the grid still reads as deliberate; do not claim frame-accurate beat sync, and do not build anything that breaks visibly if the music is 2 BPM off.

DERIVE THE GRID: beat = 60 / BPM seconds. Bar = 4 beats. At 128 BPM that is 0.469s per beat, 1.875s per bar. Section boundaries land on BARS. Accents (a card snapping in, a number ticking over, a colour flip) land on BEATS or eighths (half a beat). Nothing lands on an arbitrary timestamp — if a section wants to be 'about 3 seconds', make it exactly 2 bars.

SECTION LENGTH IS IN BARS, NOT SECONDS. Two bars is the default section. Four bars only for a section that genuinely carries more information. One bar for a hit or a flash cut. A 15-second piece at 128 BPM is 8 bars total — that is four 2-bar sections, not three vague 5-second slides.

NO DEAD AIR. See skills/animation-sections — every section must keep something in continuous motion for its entire span. A section that animates in over 10 frames and then sits still for 2 seconds is the single biggest quality defect in this pipeline. Fixing it is worth more than any amount of styling.

CLIP LENGTH: lyria-3-clip-preview returns roughly 30s. For a piece longer than the returned clip, either generate a second clip and butt them on the audio track at a bar boundary, or loop the first — never let the bed run out mid-video. Read the emitted path from the step output; the extension is advisory and the file is whatever container Lyria returned (mp3 in practice).

ATTACH THE BED: set project.audio.tracks to one entry for the generated file — { id: 'music', src: <abs path from step output>, start: 0, end: <video duration>, volume: 1.0, label: 'music' }. Use montaj probe for the clip's real duration. An animations project has no dialogue, so no ducking is needed; leave it off unless the prompt adds narration.

60 FPS: canvas projects now init at 60fps (project/init.py). Author every interpolate() and spring() against the project's real fps — read it from settings.fps rather than assuming 30, or every animation runs at half the intended speed. A 10-frame ease at 60fps is 167ms, not 333ms.

SILENT PIECES: if the prompt explicitly asks for no music (a bed will be added later, or the piece is meant to sit silent in a feed), skip the music step — but STILL pick a notional BPM and cut to that grid. The rhythm is what makes it read as designed; the audio is what makes it read as finished.

TRACKS[0] stays empty — the schema requires tracks[0] items be type 'video' and an animation project has no footage. Primary visual layer is tracks[1]. See skills/animation-sections for the opaque/crossfade mechanics.
